correctness.rationale: Direct Cayley--Dickson multiplication gives Im(Phi) contained in W=(Fp0+Fn0) plus M2(F)omega. For x0=E11+E21, the slice y -> Phi(x0,y) has quaternion coordinates (a11-a21-a22,a12,0,0) and omega coordinates (b11+b12,b12,b21+b22,b22). The resulting six-coordinate map has determinant 1, hence is onto W over every field; equality follows. The hypotheses place p0,n0 among linearly independent zero divisors with polar norm zero.

value.rationale: The standard pair p0,n0 is fixed by the motivating paper itself and sits inside the paper's only unresolved image-structure case. Showing that its nonlinear two-variable image is exactly a six-dimensional subspace, and that one fixed linear slice already fills that subspace, gives a natural structural base case for studying the exceptional octonion regime rather than an arbitrary coordinate computation.
